title: A positive genotype-phenotype correlation in a large cohort of patients with Pseudohypoparathyroidism Type Ia and Pseudo-pseudohypoparathyroidism and 33 newly identified mutations in the GNAS gene.

reviewer.method: Direct full source reading and visual inspection where recorded; item-by-item selected/alternate packet comparison. Mechanical extraction/inventory is not read credit.

audit.exposure_note: Required full HANDOFF.md read on 2026-10-24 exposed aggregate source-audit counts, HG002/HG001/phenotype-only top1/5/10 summaries, compact 556/653/665 versus 430/649/665 of 681, corrected deltas, and the historical public FGFR2 rank 1 at 0.9654. Conservatively per_case, not blinded. No case ranking/outcome files were consulted for this review; only assigned source contexts, identities, availability, held primary sources and the adjudication validator were used.

components.note: Primary XML supplementary-material @id=sd1; Table S1. Genotype and phenotype of patients with PHPIa, PPHP, and POH harboring inactivating mutations in the GNAS gene. Table S1 summarizes age at diagnosis, sex, PHP subtype, AHO signs, laboratory diagnostics, Gsα protein activity, endocrinopathies, the identified GNAS mutation on nucleotide and on peptide level (based on the RefSeq NM_001077488.1) and the pattern of inheritance of our patients

limitations: Source transcript numbering differs explicitly; not automatically a different allele.

patient_identity.statement: P69 is female aged 17y11m, PHPIa, matching identifier and sex. Source age is age at diagnosis, not explicitly last encounter.

evidence.locator: S1 page 3, P69 row and table footnotes

genotype.statement: Source P69 has c.757_759delAGC, p.S253del on NM_001077488.1. Packet c.754_756del/p.Ser252del on NM_000516.7 is consistent with the one-amino-acid/three-base transcript offset explicitly discussed in Methods.

evidence.locator: Methods Statistical/structural analysis and S1 P69

limitations: Exact hg38 left-normalization and transcript version .7 not independently verified from this article.

segregation.statement: P69 inheritance is labeled de novo in S1. Main Results describes de novo as mother or father not bearing the variant, without patient-specific parental assay/paternity detail.

evidence.locator: S1 page 3, P69 row and table footnotes

limitations: Table label retained; both-parent confirmation cannot be independently reconstructed.

phase.statement: Single heterozygous variant; cis/trans pairing inapplicable. PHPIa/imprinting biology does not independently demonstrate maternal chromosomal origin for this de novo event.
limitations: Parental homolog of de novo variant not directly phased.

causal_confidence.statement: PHPIa attribution is supported by PTH/TSH resistance and patient erythrocyte Gsalpha activity 42% (reference 85-115%); no separate functional assay of the isolated P69 deletion is reported.

evidence.locator: S1 page 3, P69 row and table footnotes

limitations: Patient-level activity and study attribution are not independent pathogenicity recertification.
